# app/controllers/api/v1/documents_controller.rb
class Api::V1::DocumentsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_api_key!
  before_action :load_document, only: [:show, :update, :destroy]

  # GET /api/v1/documents/:id
  def show
    render json: @document.as_json(include: :metadata)
  end

  # POST /api/v1/documents
  def create
    @document = Document.new(document_params)
    @document.owner_id = current_api_user.id
    
    if @document.save
      AuditLog.create!(
        action: 'document_created',
        resource_id: @document.id,
        resource_type: 'Document',
        actor_id: current_api_user.id,
        metadata: { ip: request.remote_ip, ua: request.user_agent }
      )
      render json: @document, status: :created
    else
      render json: { errors: @document.errors.full_messages }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # PATCH /api/v1/documents/:id
  def update
    old_attrs = @document.attributes.slice('title', 'content', 'classification')
    
    if @document.update(document_params)
      AuditLog.create!(
        action: 'document_updated',
        resource_id: @document.id,
        resource_type: 'Document',
        actor_id: current_api_user.id,
        metadata: { changes: old_attrs, ip: request.remote_ip }
      )
      render json: @document
    else
      render json: { errors: @document.errors.full_messages }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # DELETE /api/v1/documents/:id
  def destroy
    @document.destroy!
    AuditLog.create!(
      action: 'document_deleted',
      resource_id: params[:id],
      resource_type: 'Document',
      actor_id: current_api_user.id,
      metadata: { ip: request.remote_ip }
    )
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def load_document
    @document = Document.find_by(id: params[:id])
    # No nil check - relies on downstream .as_json / .update / .destroy
    # to raise NoMethodError on nil if document not found
  end

  def document_params
    params.require(:document).permit(:title, :content, :classification, :department_id)
  end

  def authenticate_api_key!
    api_key = request.headers['X-API-Key']
    @current_api_user = ApiUser.find_by(key: api_key, active: true)
    unless @current_api_user
      render json: { error: 'Unauthorized' }, status: :unauthorized
    end
  end

  def current_api_user
    @current_api_user
  end
end

# app/models/document.rb
class Document < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :owner, class_name: 'ApiUser'
  belongs_to :department, optional: true
  has_one :metadata, class_name: 'DocumentMetadata', dependent: :destroy

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :classification, inclusion: { in: %w[public internal confidential secret] }

  after_create :initialize_metadata

  private

  def initialize_metadata
    DocumentMetadata.create!(document: self, version: 1, checksum: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(content.to_s))
  end
end

environment.description: Rails 7.1 API deployed on EC2 with PostgreSQL 15. The application database user 'railsapp' has full DML privileges (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) on all tables. No authorization layer beyond API key authentication. Application runs in production mode with config.consider_all_requests_local = false. The null pointer dereference (NoMethodError on nil) when accessing non-existent document IDs causes a 500 error that leaks no stack trace, but the real vulnerability is that any authenticated API user can modify or delete ANY document regardless of ownership since there's no authorization check in load_document. Combined with the nil dereference, attackers can enumerate valid document IDs (200 vs 500) and then modify/delete documents belonging to other users.
